headline: Indonesia Lifts Its Benchmark Rate to 6%
deck: Bank Indonesia also raised its deposit and lending facility rates as it sought to stabilise the rupiah amid global uncertainty.
body: Bank Indonesia lifted its benchmark BI Rate by 25 basis points to 6.00% at its 17–18 November meeting. It also raised the Deposit Facility rate to 5.25% and the Lending Facility rate to 6.75%. [E1] [E4] [E5] [E7] [E10]

Bank Indonesia said the increase was intended to strengthen rupiah stabilisation amid rising global uncertainty and to keep 2026–27 inflation within its 2.5% ±1 percentage-point target range. Governor Destry Damayanti gave the same rationale at a news conference. [E2] [E6] [E8]

The bank put the rupiah at Rp18,245 per U.S. dollar on 17 November, 0.66% weaker than at the end of October. CNN Indonesia reported that this was Bank Indonesia’s third rate increase of 2026, after increases in May and June. [E3] [E11]

Warta Ekonomi reported that Indonesia’s economy grew 5.47% year on year in the third quarter and that October inflation was 3.23%. Damayanti also said the decision came with stronger hedging incentives for domestic non-deliverable forwards. [E9] [E12]
